claim: Each nucleosome is defined as an octamer of histone proteins wrapped by approximately 147 base pairs of genomic DNA.
source: Each nucleosome is defined as an octamer of histone proteins, which is wrapped by approximately 147 base pairs of genomic DNA (Luger et al., 1997; Kornberg, 1974).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Luger et al., 1997; Kornberg, 1974).

claim: The specific positioning of nucleosomes on DNA can have significant effects on downstream processes such as promoter accessibility and molecular recruitment, which ultimately alter gene expression.
source: The specific positioning of nucleosomes on the underlying DNA can have significant effects on downstream processes, such as promoter accessibility and molecular recruitment, which ultimately serve to alter gene expression (Lai and Pugh, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lai and Pugh, 2017.

claim: Nucleosome positioning is dynamically established by ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling proteins (ChRPs).
source: Nucleosome positioning is dynamically established by a group of enzymes known as ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling proteins (ChRPs) (Zhou et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhou et al., 2016.

claim: The CHD and ISWI families of ChRPs have been characterized as nonspecific nucleosome sliding and spacing factors in vitro.
source: The chromodomain-helicase-DNA binding (CHD) and imitation switch (ISWI) families of ChRPs have been characterized as nonspecific nucleosome sliding and spacing factors in vitro (Stockdale et al., 2006; Hauk et al., 2010; McKnight et al., 2011; Kagalwala et al., 2004; Lusser et al., 2005; Tsukiyama et al., 1999; Pointner et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: ChRPs generate evenly spaced nucleosome arrays at transcription start sites and organize genomic chromatin at other defined boundaries in yeast, flies, and mammals.
source: In yeast, flies, and mammals, ChRPs generate evenly spaced nucleosome arrays at transcription start sites and organize genomic chromatin at other defined boundaries (Pointner et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2007; Mavrich et al., 2008a; Valouev et al., 2011; Krietenstein et al., 2016; Wiechens et al., 2016; Baldi et al., 2018; Gkikopoulos et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: A widely accepted model is that ChRPs pack nucleosome arrays against a noninteracting barrier, such as an unrelated DNA binding protein or another nucleosome.
source: A widely accepted model is that ChRPs pack nucleosome arrays against a noninteracting barrier, such as an unrelated DNA binding protein or another nucleosome (Krietenstein et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2011; Mavrich et al., 2008b).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Nucleosome arrays near GRFs and other DNA binding elements appear to be phased relative to the binding motifs of sequence-specific DNA binding factors in cells and in biochemically reconstituted cell-free systems.
source: In support of this model, nucleosome arrays near GRFs and other DNA binding elements appear to be phased relative to the binding motifs of the sequence-specific DNA binding factors in cells and in biochemically reconstituted cell-free systems (Krietenstein et al., 2016; Baldi et al., 2018; Yan et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Members of the ISWI family of ChRPs functionally interact with transcription factors in vivo.
source: It has been shown through genetic and recent biochemical experiments that members of the ISWI family of ChRPs functionally interact with transcription factors in vivo (Krietenstein et al., 2016; Gelbart et al., 2005; Goldmark et al., 2000; Fazzio et al., 2001; Yadon et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Ume6 and Isw2 share genetic targets of repression and likely interact physically.
source: It has been previously demonstrated that Ume6 and Isw2, an ISWI-containing ChRP complex in Saccharomyces cerevisiae (homologous to the ATP-dependent chromatin assembly factor [ACF] complex in humans and flies), share genetic targets of repression and likely interact physically (Goldmark et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Goldmark et al., 2000.

claim: Isw2 activity is specialized at only a subset of target sites.
source: When examining the positioning of nucleosomes with and without Isw2 at all yeast pre-initiation complex sites (PICs), it is evident that Isw2 activity is specialized at only a subset of target sites (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: No global nucleosome spacing or organizing activity is detected by Isw2 alone.
source: As seen previously (Gkikopoulos et al., 2011; Ocampo et al., 2016), no global nucleosome spacing or organizing activity is detected by Isw2 alone (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and citations to prior work.

claim: Isw2 can only organize a single PIC-proximal nucleosome, while subsequent nucleosomes become more poorly phased as the distance from the initially positioned nucleosome increases.
source: Close inspection of Isw2-targeted PICs suggests that Isw2 can only organize a single PIC-proximal nucleosome, while subsequent nucleosomes become more poorly phased as the distance from the initially positioned nucleosome increases (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: PICs that display specific Isw2-directed activity are bound by Isw2, while those lacking any detectable nucleosome organization by Isw2 are unbound.
source: Importantly, the PICs that display specific Isw2-directed activity are bound by Isw2, while those lacking any detectable nucleosome organization by Isw2 are unbound (Figure 1A, middle panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A, middle panel.

claim: Isw2 is efficient at positioning the Ume6-proximal nucleosome but positioning of nucleosomes decays rapidly as the distance from the proximal nucleosome increases.
source: Again, we determined that Isw2 is efficient at positioning the Ume6-proximal nucleosome but positioning of nucleosomes decays rapidly as the distance from the proximal nucleosome increases, suggesting that Isw2 may only position single nucleosomes at target sites (Figure 1B, clusters 1 and 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Nucleosomes appear to always be positioned toward Ume6 motifs as nucleosome positions in the absence of Isw2 are always more distal to the Ume6 motif than when Isw2 is present.
source: Nucleosomes also appear to always be positioned toward Ume6 motifs as nucleosome positions in the absence of Isw2 are always more distal to the Ume6 motif than when Isw2 is present.
evidence: The claim is based on observations from nucleosome positioning data.

claim: Nucleosomes are positioned with the dyad only separated from the Ume6 motif by 100 nucleotides rather than the ~200 nucleotides that would be expected between dyads in a nucleosome array based on Isw2 preferentially leaving 60 base pairs of linker DNA between nucleosomes in vitro.
source: Finally, these nucleosomes are positioned with the dyad only separated from the Ume6 motif by 100 nucleotides rather than the ~200 nucleotides that would be expected between dyads in a nucleosome array based on Isw2 preferentially leaving 60 base pairs of linker DNA between nucleosomes in vitro (Kagalwala et al., 2004; Tsukiyama et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by data and citations to prior work.

claim: Isw2 does not appear to have any activity on global Ume6-proximal nucleosomes in the presence of the Ume6 DNA binding domain alone as nucleosomes in this strain occupy identical positions when Ume6 or Isw2 are completely absent.
source: However, Isw2 does not appear to have any activity on global Ume6-proximal nucleosomes in the presence of the Ume6 DNA binding domain alone as nucleosomes in this strain occupy identical positions when Ume6 or Isw2 are completely absent (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In the presence of full-length Ume6, the Isw2 complex appears to be necessary and sufficient for moving motif-proximal nucleosomes as nucleosome positions in the ISW2/isw1/chd1 strain could achieve identical motif-proximal nucleosome positions as the wild-type strain.
source: In the presence of full-length Ume6, the Isw2 complex appears to be necessary and sufficient for moving motif-proximal nucleosomes as nucleosome positions in the ISW2/isw1/chd1 strain could achieve identical motif-proximal nucleosome positions as the wild-type strain.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from nucleosome positioning experiments.

claim: The CHD1/isw1/isw2 and ISW1/chd1/isw2 strains were unable to move any Ume6-proximal nucleosomes.
source: Additionally, the CHD1/isw1/isw2 and ISW1/chd1/isw2 strains were unable to move any Ume6-proximal nucleosomes (Figure 1—figure supplements 4 and 5), which strongly argues that Ume6 is not acting as a passive barrier against which nucleosome spacing factors can pack nucleosomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 4 and 5.

claim: Deletion of residues 2–479 preserved Isw2-positioned nucleosomes at Ume6 sites, while an internal deletion of 480–507 in the context of an otherwise full-length Ume6 abrogated nucleosome positioning by Isw2.
source: Deletion of residues 2–479 preserved Isw2-positioned nucleosomes at Ume6 sites, while an internal deletion of 480–507 in the context of an otherwise full-length Ume6 abrogated nucleosome positioning by Isw2 (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ume6 ∆2–479 and Ume6 ∆2–508 showed identical binding as measured by ChIP, indicating that the loss of nucleosome positioning is not due to the loss of Ume6 binding.
source: Importantly, Ume6 ∆2–479 and Ume6 ∆2–508 showed identical binding as measured by ChIP (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), indicating that the loss of nucleosome positioning is not due to the loss of Ume6 binding.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Transcription was modestly increased at Ume6 targets in Ume6(∆2–508)/RPD3+ compared to Ume6(∆2–479)/RPD3+, which would be expected if only Isw2 is lost when residues 479–508 are deleted.
source: Transcription was modestly increased at Ume6 targets in Ume6(∆2–508)/RPD3+ compared to Ume6(∆2–479)/RPD3+ (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), which would be expected if only Isw2 is lost when residues 479–508 are deleted.
evidence: The claim is supported by transcription data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Only a modest increase in transcription was seen at Ume6 targets in the Ume6(∆2–479)/∆rpd3 strain, suggesting that Isw2 is still present, while the Ume6(∆2–508)/∆rpd3 strain displayed extreme induction of Ume6-regulated genes, suggesting that both Isw2 and Rpd3 activity are absent.
source: More convincingly, only a modest increase in transcription was seen at Ume6 targets in the Ume6(∆2–479)/∆rpd3 strain, suggesting that Isw2 is still present, while the Ume6(∆2–508)/∆rpd3 strain displayed extreme induction of Ume6-regulated genes, suggesting that both Isw2 and Rpd3 activity are absent (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcription data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: The fusion protein with ectopically displayed Ume6 residues 479–508 was capable of fully recapitulating Isw2-positioned nucleosomes at a subset of Ume6 sites.
source: This fusion protein was capable of fully recapitulating Isw2-positioned nucleosomes at a subset of Ume6 sites (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplements 6 and 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplements 6 and 7.

claim: The region spanning residues 479–508 in Ume6 is a yeast-conserved Isw2-recruitment domain and is required and sufficient for recruiting Isw2 nucleosome positioning activity to Ume6 targets.
source: We conclude that the region spanning residues 479–508 in Ume6 is a yeast-conserved Isw2-recruitment domain and is required and sufficient for recruiting Isw2 nucleosome positioning activity to Ume6 targets.
evidence: The claim is based on the results from truncation and ectopic display experiments.

claim: Deletion of the MBP1 gene resulted in ectopic nucleosome positioning at a subset of Mbp1 target loci, which was identical to mispositioned nucleosomes in a ∆isw2 strain.
source: While dissecting the Isw2-recruitment domain in Ume6, we discovered that deleting the MBP1 gene resulted in ectopic nucleosome positioning at a subset of Mbp1 target loci, which was identical to mispositioned nucleosomes in a ∆isw2 strain.
evidence: The claim is supported by nucleosome positioning data.

claim: Deletion of the SWI6 gene led to ectopic nucleosome positions identical to ∆mbp1 and ∆isw2 strains at the small subset of Mbp1 targets.
source: As predicted, deletion of the SWI6 gene led to ectopic nucleosome positions identical to ∆mbp1 and ∆isw2 strains at the small subset of Mbp1 targets.
evidence: The claim is supported by nucleosome positioning data.

claim: Ectopic nucleosome positioning was observed at the HSP12 locus (an SBF target) when either Isw2, Swi6, or Swi4 was absent.
source: Indeed, we observed ectopic nucleosome positioning at the HSP12 locus (an SBF target) when either Isw2, Swi6, or Swi4 was absent (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Wild-type nucleosome positions were observed in the absence of Mbp1, indicating that this is specific to SBF.
source: Wild-type nucleosome positions were observed in the absence of Mbp1, indicating that this is specific to SBF.
evidence: The claim is supported by nucleosome positioning data.

claim: Wild-type nucleosome positions were observed at Mbp1 targets when Swi4 was missing, suggesting that MBF and SBF have individual Isw2-targeting capacity at their respective binding sites.
source: Similarly, wild-type nucleosome positions were observed at Mbp1 targets when Swi4 was missing (Figure 3A), again suggesting that MBF and SBF have individual Isw2-targeting capacity at their respective binding sites.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Swi6 appears to be an adapter protein responsible for recruiting Isw2 to Mbp1 and Swi4 sites since Swi6 has no intrinsic DNA binding domain.
source: Swi6 appears to be an adapter protein responsible for recruiting Isw2 to Mbp1 and Swi4 sites since Swi6 has no intrinsic DNA binding domain.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the data and knowledge about Swi6.

claim: Introduction of the SpyCatcher-Ume6 fusion to the Mbp1(1–136)-SpyTag background resulted in the rescue of proper Isw2-directed nucleosome positioning at Mbp1 sites.
source: We then introduced SpyCatcher fused to the helical element from Ume6, which was characterized above for bringing Isw2 to Ume6-bound loci. Introduction of the SpyCatcher-Ume6 fusion to the Mbp1(1–136)-SpyTag background resulted in the rescue of proper Isw2-directed nucleosome positioning at Mbp1 sites (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Isw2 containing Itc1(∆2–374) did not display any defects in nucleosome sliding using a gel mobility shift assay that detects nucleosome centering by Isw2.
source: Isw2 containing Itc1(∆2–374) did not display any defects in nucleosome sliding using a gel mobility shift assay that detects nucleosome centering by Isw2 (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The Itc1(∆2–374) construct was not lethal in the W303 background, but phenocopied a ∆isw2 strain by displaying identical ectopic nucleosome positioning at all Isw2 target sites throughout the genome.
source: Surprisingly, this construct was not lethal in our W303 background, but phenocopied a ∆isw2 strain by displaying identical ectopic nucleosome positioning at all Isw2 target sites throughout the genome (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Deletion of the WAC domain (Itc1 residues 24–130) produced identically ectopic nucleosome positions compared to ∆isw2 at target loci and genome-wide.
source: Deletion of the WAC domain (Itc1 residues 24–130) produced identically ectopic nucleosome positions compared to ∆isw2 at target loci (Figure 4C) and genome-wide (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4D.

claim: The WAC domain of Itc1 is the component of the Isw2 complex responsible for coupling with epitopes on DNA-bound factors such as Ume6, Swi6, and all other Isw2 targeting proteins with yet-to-be-defined recruitment epitopes.
source: We conclude that the WAC domain of Itc1 is the component of the Isw2 complex responsible for coupling with epitopes on DNA-bound factors such as Ume6, Swi6, and all other Isw2 targeting proteins with yet-to-be-defined recruitment epitopes.
evidence: The claim is based on the results from truncation experiments.

claim: Genome-wide binding demonstrates large, but not complete overlap of Isw2(K215R)-FLAG ChIP peaks with both Itc1(1–73)-FLAG and Itc1(1–132)-FLAG, strongly suggesting that the Itc1 region from 1 to 73 alone can interact with Isw2 targets.
source: Genome-wide binding demonstrates large, but not complete overlap of Isw2(K215R)-FLAG ChIP peaks with both Itc1(1–73)-FLAG and Itc1(1–132)-FLAG, strongly suggesting that the Itc1 region from 1 to 73 alone can interact with Isw2 targets.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data.

claim: The Itc1 signal and Isw2 signal were offset at target genes such that Itc1(1–73) or Itc1(1–132) was upstream and Isw2 was closer to the nucleosome that was selected for repositioning.
source: We noticed that the Itc1 signal and Isw2 signal were offset at target genes such that Itc1(1–73) or Itc1(1–132) was upstream and Isw2 was closer to the nucleosome that was selected for repositioning (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Itc1(1–73) was associated with approximately half of Isw2-bound loci and was offset from the catalytic subunit at all co-bound sites.
source: Genome-wide analysis showed that Itc1(1–73) was associated with approximately half of Isw2-bound loci and was offset from the catalytic subunit at all co-bound sites (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: In all cases, Itc1(1–73) was found upstream of the nucleosome that was repositioned, and Isw2 was located on top of the selected nucleosome.
source: In all cases, Itc1(1–73) was found upstream of the nucleosome that was repositioned, and Isw2 was located on top of the selected nucleosome.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data.

claim: Nucleosomes were always shifted toward the Itc1 subunit.
source: Nucleosomes were always shifted toward the Itc1 subunit (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The Drosophila genus underwent reversal or loss of negative charge at multiple residues that are strictly or mostly acidic in other representative organisms.
source: While sequence alignment demonstrated widespread conservation of the WAC domain, one striking feature was exposed: the Drosophila genus underwent reversal or loss of negative charge at multiple residues that are strictly or mostly acidic in other representative organisms (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The E33R/E40H double mutation (a, b) was enough to completely abolish Isw2 activity at specific and known Isw2 targets and at all genomic loci where Isw2 activity is observed.
source: Strikingly, the E33R/E40H double mutation (a, b) was enough to completely abolish Isw2 activity at specific and known Isw2 targets (Figure 6B) and at all genomic loci where Isw2 activity is observed (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6C.

claim: Mutation of the less-conserved acidic residues E43R/D70K (c, d) retained Isw2-directed nucleosome positioning.
source: Mutation of the less-conserved acidic residues E43R/D70K (c, d) retained Isw2-directed nucleosome positioning.
evidence: The claim is supported by nucleosome positioning data.

claim: Mutation of all four acidic residues (a, b, c, d) E33R/E40H/E43R/D70K resulted in complete loss of Isw2-targeted activity across the genome.
source: As expected, mutation of all four acidic residues (a, b, c, d) E33R/E40H/E43R/D70K resulted in complete loss of Isw2-targeted activity across the genome (Figure 6B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6C.

claim: The Drosophila genus lost critical acidic residues that are essential for targeted nucleosome positioning by S. cerevisiae Isw2, potentially explaining the disconnect between the Drosophila ACF literature and what we have characterized herein.
source: We conclude that the Drosophila genus lost critical acidic residues that are essential for targeted nucleosome positioning by S. cerevisiae Isw2, potentially explaining the disconnect between the Drosophila ACF literature and what we have characterized herein.
evidence: The claim is based on the results from charge reversal experiments and sequence alignment.

claim: There is strong potential that humans and most other organisms have retained targeting potential as they retain mechanistically important acidic residues present in yeast Itc1.
source: We also believe that there is strong potential that humans and most other organisms have retained targeting potential as they retain mechanistically important acidic residues present in yeast Itc1.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence conservation analysis.

claim: Targeted nucleosome array formation has previously been observed in humans at specific transcription factor sites including CTCF, JUN, and RFX5.
source: In support of conservation, targeted nucleosome array formation has previously been observed in humans at specific transcription factor sites including CTCF, JUN, and RFX5 (Wiechens et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wiechens et al., 2016.

claim: Isw2 has been characterized extensively in biochemical assays, which all suggest that it has nonspecific DNA binding, ATP hydrolysis, nucleosome sliding, mononucleosome centering, and nucleosome spacing activities.
source: Yeast Isw2 has been characterized extensively in biochemical assays, which all suggest that it has nonspecific DNA binding, ATP hydrolysis, nucleosome sliding, mononucleosome centering, and nucleosome spacing activities (Stockdale et al., 2006; Kagalwala et al., 2004; Lusser et al., 2005; Tsukiyama et al., 1999; Dang and Bartholomew, 2007; Dang et al., 2006; Hota et al., 2013; Kassabov et al., 2002; Zofall et al., 2004; Zofall et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: It is estimated that there are enough Isw2 molecules for every 10–20 nucleosomes in the genome.
source: These nonspecific nucleosome mobilizing activities suggest that the Isw2 protein should be able to organize nucleosome arrays against a barrier across the genome in yeast cells since (1) it is estimated that there are enough Isw2 molecules for every 10–20 nucleosomes in the genome (Gelbart et al., 2005)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gelbart et al., 2005.

claim: Drosophila melanogaster ACF, an Isw2 ortholog, can organize nucleosomes into evenly spaced arrays.
source: (2) Drosophila melanogaster ACF, an Isw2 ortholog, can organize nucleosomes into evenly spaced arrays (Baldi et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Baldi et al., 2018.

claim: Other nonspecific and related nucleosome spacing factors can globally space nucleosomes across the genome in yeast and other organisms.
source: (3) other nonspecific and related nucleosome spacing factors can globally space nucleosomes across the genome in yeast and other organisms (Pointner et al., 2012; Wiechens et al., 2016; Gkikopoulos et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Isw2 activity at Ume6-bound loci has been previously characterized as precise, with Isw2 reproducibly moving nucleosomes until the predicted edge of the nucleosome core particle is 30 base pairs from the center of the Ume6 binding motif.
source: Isw2 activity at Ume6-bound loci has been previously characterized as precise, with Isw2 reproducibly moving nucleosomes until the predicted edge of the nucleosome core particle is 30 base pairs from the center of the Ume6 binding motif (McKnight et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to McKnight et al., 2016.

claim: Mbp1 is a conserved cell cycle regulator that complexes with Swi6 to form the MBF complex.
source: Mbp1 is a conserved cell cycle regulator that complexes with Swi6 to form the MBF complex (Koch et al., 1993).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Koch et al., 1993.

claim: The MBF complex activates the transition from G1 to S and includes the conserved function of regulating Start-specific transcription.
source: This complex activates the transition from G1 to S and includes the conserved function of regulating Start-specific transcription (Koch et al., 1993; Breeden, 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Koch et al., 1993 and Breeden, 1996.

claim: The DNA binding element in Mbp1 resides in the extreme N-terminus spanning residues 2–124.
source: The DNA binding element in Mbp1 resides in the extreme N-terminus (Figure 3A) spanning residues 2–124 (Nair et al., 2003)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nair et al., 2003 and Figure 3A.

claim: The ~350 amino acid N-terminal region of human Acf1 was shown to bind both extranucleosomal linker DNA and the histone H4 tail, suggesting an allosteric mechanism through which ISWI complexes can set proper spacing between nucleosomes.
source: The ~350 amino acid N-terminal region of human Acf1 was shown to bind both extranucleosomal linker DNA and the histone H4 tail, suggesting an allosteric mechanism through which ISWI complexes can set proper spacing between nucleosomes (Hwang et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hwang et al., 2014.

claim: Hwang et al. demonstrated that removal of residues 2–374 in S. cerevisiae was lethal, suggesting a critical and conserved role of these residues in establishing proper chromatin structure in vivo.
source: Though this work was performed with human ACF complex, Hwang et al. demonstrated that removal of residues 2–374 in S. cerevisiae was lethal, suggesting a critical and conserved role of these residues in establishing proper chromatin structure in vivo (Hwang et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hwang et al., 2014.

claim: ISWI proteins were shown to move nucleosomes away from inert DNA-bound factors.
source: Similarly, these specific movements toward Ume6 (a barrier) are inconsistent with previous biophysical studies, where ISWI proteins were shown to move nucleosomes away from inert DNA-bound factors (Li et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2015.

claim: Artificially tethered chromatin remodeling proteins were previously shown to always move nucleosomes toward target sites.
source: Consistent with this immobilized pulling model and consistent with the directional movement of single nucleosomes toward Ume6-bound sites, artificially tethered chromatin remodeling proteins were previously shown to always move nucleosomes toward target sites (Donovan et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Donovan et al., 2019.

claim: Isw2 is in a globally repressed state in cells and activated solely on target nucleosomes.
source: We therefore speculate that Isw2 is in a globally repressed state in cells and activated solely on target nucleosomes.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the observed data.

claim: An unknown inhibitory factor that interacts with Isw2 or the nucleosome in cells may be lost during protein purification, allowing for the ubiquitous Isw2 chromatin remodeling activity observed in vitro.
source: For example, an unknown inhibitory factor that interacts with Isw2 or the nucleosome in cells may be lost during protein purification, allowing for the ubiquitous Isw2 chromatin remodeling activity observed in vitro.
evidence: The claim is speculative.

claim: It is conceivable that Isw2 is unable to bind to linker DNA the same way in a genomic context as it can bind in vitro, potentially due to the presence of unknown chromatin interacting components, molecular crowding, chromatin folding, or other physiological differences not recapitulated in vitro.
source: Additionally, it is conceivable that Isw2 is unable to bind to linker DNA the same way in a genomic context as it can bind in vitro, potentially due to the presence of unknown chromatin interacting components, molecular crowding, chromatin folding, or other physiological differences not recapitulated in vitro.
evidence: The claim is speculative.

claim: The increase in positive charge in Drosophila may simultaneously increase nonspecific binding of Drosophila Acf1 to extranucleosomal DNA, and these charge reversals may help explain the nonspecific spacing behavior of Acf1 observed in Drosophila.
source: It is possible that the increase in positive charge simultaneously increases nonspecific binding of Drosophila Acf1 to extranucleosomal DNA, and these charge reversals may help explain the nonspecific spacing behavior of Acf1 observed in Drosophila.
evidence: The claim is speculative.

claim: If the Itc1 N-terminus can bind H4 tail and transcription factor epitopes similarly to extranucleosomal DNA and H4 tail, the Hwang et al. model can mechanistically explain the precise distance measurements made at targeted sites in cells.
source: If the Itc1 N-terminus can bind H4 tail and transcription factor epitopes similarly to extranucleosomal DNA and H4 tail, the Hwang et al. model (Hwang et al., 2014) can mechanistically explain the precise distance measurements made at targeted sites in cells.
evidence: The claim is speculative and based on inference from the Hwang et al. model.

claim: In this speculative model, Itc1 binds a targeting epitope at a genomic locus when the upstream nucleosome is far away.
source: In this speculative model, Itc1 binds a targeting epitope at a genomic locus when the upstream nucleosome is far away.
evidence: The claim is speculative.

claim: When the length between the nucleosome and the recruiting epitope is short enough, the Itc1 N-terminus may bind the H4 tail to inactivate Isw2 through autoinhibition.
source: When the length between the nucleosome and the recruiting epitope is short enough, the Itc1 N-terminus may bind the H4 tail to inactivate Isw2 through autoinhibition.
evidence: The claim is speculative.

claim: An interacting barrier can behave directionally while a non-interacting barrier cannot.
source: First, an interacting barrier can behave directionally while a non-interacting barrier cannot.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the data.

claim: An interacting barrier can be modulated in a condition-specific manner through post-translational modification of the small epitope on the Isw2-recruitment factor.
source: Second, an interacting barrier can be modulated in a condition-specific manner through post-translational modification of the small epitope on the Isw2-recruitment factor.
evidence: The claim is based on inference and speculation.

claim: Only three Swi6-regulated genes were identified as Swi6-mediated Isw2-recruitment sites.
source: Interestingly, only three Swi6-regulated genes were identified as Swi6-mediated Isw2-recruitment sites.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: It is likely that the Swi6–Isw2 interaction can be tuned by cellular context.
source: It is thus likely that the Swi6–Isw2 interaction can be tuned by cellular context, which is not possible for noninteracting barriers.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the data.

claim: Other targeting factors likely exist, which might recruit the Isw2 complex to specific sites in the genome through a variety of different domains.
source: We predict that other targeting factors likely exist, which might recruit the Isw2 complex to specific sites in the genome through a variety of different domains, and that this creates a mechanism by which remodeling occurs at specific subsets of genomic loci in response to the presence of these recruitment factors.
